meeting_summary.brief: The team presented and evaluated a physical prototype for a new remote control. The primary focus was a feature trade-off analysis to reduce the production cost from an initial 13.7 euros to below the 12.5 euro target. The team successfully met the budget by changing the case material from rubber to plastic while retaining key innovative features like a kinetic power source and voice recognition.

requirements.title: Curved Casing
requirements.statement: The product casing SHALL have curved sides.
acceptance_criteria: The physical product casing must exhibit a continuous curve along its vertical edges.
The design must also feature a curve leading up to the main display area.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_C introduced the prototype's physical design (enthusiastic, conf=0.7), specifically pointing out that the sides are slightly curved and that the curve extends up to the main display. Speaker_B expressed agreement and satisfaction with the design (satisfied, conf=0.9).

requirements.title: Hidden Function Panel
requirements.statement: The product SHALL feature a pull-down panel to conceal additional function buttons.
acceptance_criteria: A section of the remote's lower face must be a movable panel.
Actuating the panel must reveal a set of function buttons.
A visual indicator, such as a line, must be present on the panel to signify its function.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_C described the prototype's design (calm, conf=0.9), explaining that a line at the bottom indicates a panel that pulls down to reveal extra function buttons. No objections were raised.

requirements.title: Company Logo Display
requirements.statement: The product SHALL display the company logo.
acceptance_criteria: The final product must have the official company logo affixed to its casing, as represented by the sticker on the prototype.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_C stated (calm, conf=0.9) that the prototype includes a sticker with the company logo on the bottom. Speaker_B later confirmed (calm, conf=0.9) that the logo is a key part of the corporate image.

requirements.title: Cherry-Shaped Button
requirements.statement: The product SHALL include one button shaped like a cherry.
acceptance_criteria: One button on the primary interface must be physically molded in the shape of a cherry.
The design must not be confusable with the Apple Inc. logo.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B introduced an 'Apple/cherry' design (satisfied, conf=0.7). Speaker_A agreed that a cherry would be acceptable (satisfied, conf=0.9). Speaker_C supported the cherry idea as more fun and less likely to cause copyright issues with Apple Mac (enthusiastic, conf=0.8; calm, conf=0.9). The decision was confirmed later in the meeting (utterance 382).

requirements.title: Mute Button
requirements.statement: The product SHALL provide a dedicated mute button.
acceptance_criteria: A single button press must toggle the audio mute function.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B asked about a specific button on the prototype (calm, conf=0.9). Speaker_C identified it as the mute button (calm, conf=0.9).

requirements.title: Mute Button Label
requirements.statement: The mute button SHALL be labeled with the text 'mute'.
acceptance_criteria: The text 'mute' must be clearly printed on or adjacent to the mute button.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_C stated (calm, conf=0.9) that the mute button would probably have to be labeled 'mute' on the final product, explaining it was omitted from the prototype due to physical constraints.

requirements.title: Lemon-Shaped Volume Buttons
requirements.statement: The volume control buttons SHALL be shaped like lemons.
acceptance_criteria: The buttons for increasing and decreasing volume must be physically molded in the shape of lemons.
requirements.evidence: After deciding to add a second special button form to maintain the product's 'fashion' score, Speaker_A suggested lemon-shaped buttons for volume control (satisfied, conf=0.8). Speaker_D expressed strong approval (enthusiastic, conf=0.8), and the idea was accepted by the group.

requirements.title: Color-Coded Volume Buttons
requirements.statement: The volume-related buttons SHALL have a distinct color from other buttons.
acceptance_criteria: All buttons related to volume control must share a single color (e.g., orange as on the prototype) that is different from the channel buttons and the base button color.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B explained a design choice on the prototype (calm, conf=0.9), stating that volume-related buttons were separated by color (orange) from channel-related buttons to improve usability.

requirements.title: Color-Coded Channel Buttons
requirements.statement: The channel-related buttons SHALL have a distinct color from other buttons.
acceptance_criteria: All buttons related to channel control must share a single color (e.g., blue as on the prototype) that is different from the volume buttons and the base button color.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B explained a design choice on the prototype (calm, conf=0.9), stating that channel-related buttons were separated by color (blue) from volume-related buttons to improve usability.

requirements.title: Kinetic Power Source
requirements.statement: The product SHALL be powered by a kinetic energy source.
acceptance_criteria: The product must not require disposable or rechargeable batteries for its primary operation.
The product must generate and store its own power from user motion (e.g., shaking).
requirements.evidence: This feature was introduced as part of the base design (calm, conf=0.9). When discussing cost-cutting, replacing it with a battery was considered but ultimately rejected because market research indicated a strong user preference for not having to replace batteries (calm, conf=0.9). Speaker_C also argued it was more impressive than voice recognition (calm, conf=0.9). The final design retains this feature.

requirements.title: Find-My-Remote Feature
requirements.statement: The product SHALL provide a feature to help the user locate it when it is lost.
acceptance_criteria: The product must respond to a voice command from the user.
The response must be an audible or visual signal that allows the user to find the remote's physical location.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B introduced the 'sample sensor' and 'sample speaker' for voice recognition (calm, conf=0.9). Speaker_A clarified the primary purpose of this feature (calm, conf=0.9): to allow users to find the remote if it gets lost. This feature was deemed important enough to keep in the final design.

requirements.title: Plastic Casing Material
requirements.statement: The product casing SHALL be made of plastic.
acceptance_criteria: The main body of the remote control must be constructed from a plastic material.
requirements.evidence: To meet the cost target, Speaker_A identified that changing the case to plastic would provide a significant cost saving (calm, conf=0.9). Speaker_C agreed this was acceptable (calm, conf=0.9), and Speaker_B supported the change, suggesting a 'sleeker plastic case' might better fit the corporate identity (calm, conf=0.9). This was the key decision that brought the product within budget.

requirements.title: Rubber Buttons
requirements.statement: The product's buttons SHALL be made of a rubber material.
acceptance_criteria: All external buttons on the device must be manufactured from a rubber or rubber-like material, providing a soft or 'spongy' feel.
requirements.evidence: Speaker_A initially stated the design included rubber buttons (calm, conf=0.9), which Speaker_B confirmed (calm, conf=0.9). When the casing material was changed from rubber to plastic, Speaker_C noted that keeping the rubber buttons was an important factor in that decision (calm, conf=0.9).

requirements.title: Standard Hidden Panel Buttons
requirements.statement: The buttons on the hidden panel SHALL be of a standard shape and color.
acceptance_criteria: All buttons located under the slide-away panel must be small, round, and of a single, uniform color (e.g., blue).
requirements.evidence: Speaker_B raised the question of the buttons on the hidden panel (calm, conf=0.8). Speaker_C proposed that small, round, blue buttons would be sufficient (calm, conf=0.8). Speaker_D and Speaker_A agreed, reasoning that these less-used, functional buttons do not require special design elements (calm, conf=0.9; calm, conf=0.8).

non_functional_requirements.title: Production Cost Limit
non_functional_requirements.statement: The product SHALL have a total production cost under 12.50 euros.
acceptance_criteria: The final bill of materials and manufacturing cost for a single unit must be calculated as less than or equal to 12.50 euros.
non_functional_requirements.evidence: Speaker_A explicitly stated the production cost constraint from a previous meeting was to be under 12.5 euros (calm, conf=0.9). This constraint drove the entire feature trade-off discussion. The initial design cost of 13.7 caused concern (anxious, conf=0.7). The team successfully redesigned the product to a final cost of 12.3 euros, meeting the requirement (satisfied, conf=0.9).

non_functional_requirements.title: High Ease of Use
non_functional_requirements.statement: The product SHALL be easy to use.
acceptance_criteria: When evaluated on a 1-7 scale (1=True, 7=False) for the statement 'The product is easy to use', the product must score a 1.
non_functional_requirements.evidence: During the prototype evaluation, 'easy to use' was a key criterion. Speaker_A stated with high confidence that the product should score a 'one' on this metric (enthusiastic, conf=0.9), and Speaker_C agreed (calm, conf=0.9). This indicates a strong stakeholder desire for maximum ease of use.

open_issues.description: The initial prototype design had a calculated production cost of 13.7 euros, which exceeded the mandatory budget limit of 12.5 euros.
open_issues.suggested_resolution: This issue was resolved during the meeting. The team conducted a feature trade-off analysis and decided to change the casing material from rubber to plastic. This change reduced the cost to 12.3 euros, successfully bringing the product within budget.
